title: Mapping-space pullback criterion and existence of finite coherent limits
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent cones and their limiting property as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathscr E$ be a quasicategory. An object $e$ is terminal exactly when $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr E}(x,e)$ is weakly contractible for every $x$. A coherent square with vertices $p,a,b,c$, presenting a cone on $a\to c\leftarrow b$, is limiting exactly when its projection-induced comparison
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr E}(x,p)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr E}(x,a)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr E}(x,c)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr E}(x,b)$$
is an equivalence of spaces for every $x$. Here, for maps $a:A\to C$ and $b:B\to C$ of Kan complexes, $A\times_C^h B$ denotes the space modeled by $A\times_{C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,C}B$, whose points are triples $(u,v,\gamma)$ with a path $\gamma:a(u)\to b(v)$, retaining all higher simplices. The comparison retains the square's specified coherence. These criteria are invariant under equivalences of apices and of cospan diagrams, and the comparisons are natural in maps of cones. If $\mathscr E$ has a terminal object and a limiting cone on every cospan, then every diagram $K\to\mathscr E$ with $K$ a simplicial set having finitely many nondegenerate simplices has a limiting coherent cone; this is existence of finite limits.
